Parameter objects

Source: R/param.R
param.Rd

A param is a value (a number, a text, a choice, ...) together with information that describes it: a label, a help text and rules that tell whether the value is valid. Parameter UIs and reports read this information, while the functions of a pipeline always get the plain value (see param_value()).

Usage

param(
  x,
  label = "parameter",
  description = label,
  validity = default_param_validity,
  ...
)

numeric_param(
  x,
  label = "numeric parameter",
  description = label,
  min = -Inf,
  max = Inf,
  validity = .numeric_validity(min, max),
  ...
)

numeral_param(
  x,
  label = "numeral parameter",
  description = label,
  min = -Inf,
  max = Inf,
  validity = .numeral_validity(min, max),
  ...
)

choice_param(
  x,
  choices,
  label = "choice parameter",
  description = label,
  validity = .choice_validity(choices),
  ...
)

param_group(x, label = "Parameter group", description = label, ...)

Arguments

x

The value (not NULL). For choice_param() the selected choice; for param_group() a named list of params.

label

character(1) display name.

description

character(1) help text; defaults to label.

validity

A validity function or a list of them. Each function takes the plain value and returns "" if it is valid, otherwise a message (see param_validity()). See Validity for the default rules.

...

Further optional attributes as named arguments, e.g. source = "user" or advanced = TRUE (see Attributes below). Passed on to param() by the other constructors.

min, max

Inclusive bounds of the (numeric) value.

choices

The allowed values (no duplicates or NA), in the order they are shown.

Value

A param object: x with class c("param", class(x)) and the attributes. param_group() returns an object of class c("param_group", "param", "list").

Details

Constructors

  • param() creates a param of any type. The type is that of x (see param_type()), e.g. a logical becomes a switch in the UI.

The other constructors are shortcuts for common cases:

  • numeric_param(): a number (or numbers) between min and max;

  • numeral_param(): a number entered as text that keeps its decimal places, e.g. "1.50";

  • choice_param(): one of a fixed set of choices;

  • param_group(): several params shown side by side and checked together, e.g. a lower and an upper limit.

Numerals

A number like 1.50 loses its trailing zero as soon as it is a number. A numeral_param() therefore holds the text and checks it as a number (as.numeric(), without rounding).

Choices

The initial value of a choice_param() must be one of the choices (or NA). Setting a value outside the choices with param_value<- gives NA, which the validity check reports. For a simple yes/no question, a logical param (param(TRUE), shown as a switch) is often easier.

Groups

The children of a param_group() are checked on their own and the group as a whole. Add rules for the whole group with add_validity(), e.g. that a lower limit is below an upper limit (see Examples). The name "group" can't be used for a child, as it is reserved.

Validity

Each constructor comes with a default rule (see param_validity() to apply it):

ConstructorThe value is invalid if it is ...
param()empty or NA
numeric_param()empty, NA, below min or above max
numeral_param()as above, or not readable as a number
choice_param()empty or not one of the choices

Pass validity to replace the default rule (see Examples), or add further rules to an existing param with add_validity().

Working with params

Base functions such as arithmetic, comparisons, as.character(), levels() or format() work on a param as on its value. Keep in mind that arithmetic keeps the attributes and that identical(param("a"), "a") is FALSE. Pass param_value() to code that expects plain values.

Attributes

pubflow knows the following attributes. Any other named argument in ... is stored as well.

AttributeMeaning
label, descriptiondisplay name; help text (tooltip)
validitylist of validity functions
sourceorigin, e.g. "user" (set in the UI), "data" (derived from data)
areagrouping, e.g. "analysis", "criteria"
orderposition in the UI, set by param_config()
min, max, stepbounds and step of numeric inputs
advancedTRUE: shown in a collapsed "Advanced" block of the UI
lockedTRUE: shown as a disabled input, can't be changed in the UI
ui_widget, ui_args, ui_styleinput widget, its arguments and CSS

See also

param_value(), param_validity(), param_config()

Examples

# A param is its value plus information about it
p <- param("abc", label = "Name", source = "user")
p
#> param<character>: abc
#>   label: Name
#>   source: user
#>   validity: <function>
param_value(p)
#> [1] "abc"

# Numbers within bounds; params can be used like their values
alpha <- numeric_param(0.05, label = "Significance level", min = 0, max = 1)
alpha < 0.1
#> [1] TRUE
param_validity(alpha, value = 1.5)
#> [1] "value must be less than or equal to max (1)"

# A number as text keeps its trailing zero
lsl <- numeral_param("0.90", label = "LSL")
param_value(lsl)
#> [1] "0.90"

# One of several choices
trans <- choice_param("log", choices = c("none", "log", "sqrt"),
                      label = "Transformation")
levels(trans)
#> [1] "none" "log"  "sqrt"
trans == "log"
#> [1] TRUE
param_validity(trans, value = "exp")
#> [1] "value must be one of: none, log, sqrt"

# Own constructors: wrap one of the above and fix some of its arguments
yes_no_param <- function(x = c("yes", "no"), label = "Yes/No", ...) {
    choice_param(match.arg(x), choices = c("yes", "no"), label = label, ...)
}
show <- yes_no_param("no", label = "Show points?")
as.character(show)
#> [1] "no"

spec_param <- function(..., side = c("lower", "upper")) {
    numeral_param(..., side = match.arg(side))
}

# Own validity: a positive whole number. Wrap numeric_param() and pass your own
# rule; it replaces the default one, so it has to check everything it needs.
pos_integer_param <- function(
    x,
    label = "positive integer",
    description = label,
    max = .Machine$integer.max,
    validity = \(x) {
        if (length(x) == 0) return("value cannot be empty")
        if (anyNA(x)) return("value cannot be NA")
        if (any(x != round(x))) return("value must be a whole number")
        if (any(x < 1)) return("value must be positive")
        if (any(x > max)) return(paste("value must not exceed", max))
        ""
    },
    ...
) {
    numeric_param(
        x, label = label, description = description, min = 1, max = max,
        validity = validity, ...
    )
}
n <- pos_integer_param(3L, label = "Sample size")
param_validity(n, value = 2.5)
#> [1] "value must be a whole number"
param_validity(n, value = 0)
#> [1] "value must be positive"
param_validity(n)
#> [1] ""

# Params shown and checked together
limits <- param_group(
    list(
        lower = spec_param("1.0", label = "Lower", side = "lower"),
        upper = spec_param("2.0", label = "Upper", side = "upper")
    ),
    label = "Limits"
) |>
    add_validity(\(x) {
        if (as.numeric(x$lower) < as.numeric(x$upper)) "" else
            "lower must be below upper"
    })
param_validity(limits, value = list(lower = "3", upper = "2"))
#>                       group                       lower 
#> "lower must be below upper"                          "" 
#>                       upper 
#>                          ""
